1. `test_hflip_coords_transforms` - Tests that `HFlipTransform` can be instantiated with a `width` parameter and has a `width` attribute
2. `test_print_transform` - Tests that `str(HFlipTransform(width=100))` returns `'HFlipTransform(width=100)'`, which relies on `__repr__` which needs the `width` attribute to be set
3. `test_register` - Tests that `HFlipTransform(3)` can be created and has a `width` attribute accessible as `t.width`

The current implementation has `pass` in the body, which means the `width` parameter is not being stored as an attribute. Looking at the `__repr__` method in the `Transform` class, it uses `inspect.signature` to get parameter names and then uses `getattr(self, name)` to retrieve them. This means I need to set `self.width = width`.

Looking at other transform classes like `VFlipTransform`, `ScaleTransform`, etc., they all call `self._set_attributes(locals())` which sets all local variables (except those starting with `_` and `self`) as attributes on the instance.

The `HFlipTransform.__init__` should:
1. Call `super().__init__()`
2. Call `self._set_attributes(locals())` to set the `width` attribute
